newsitem.title: UK: B.Telecom to spend up to 200 mln stg on ads.
newsitem.headline: B.Telecom to spend up to 200 mln stg on ads.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc will sharply increase its advertising spending in 1997, spending up to 200 million pounds ($330 million), industry sources said on Monday.

British Telecom plans to air up to 80 television commercials in 1997 and spend up to 200 million pounds on television, press and poster advertising campaigns, industry sources told Reuters. Some of the adverts will feature former stars of the BBC soap opera Eastenders.
BT officials declined to comment on the company's advertising plans.

The company last month said it would spend about 100 million pounds on advertising in the 1996/97 financial year ending in March and would likely increase spending substantially again for the 1997/98 financial year.
BT said the advert "It's Good to Talk" with actor Bob Hoskins would be retired at the end of 1996 and would be replaced with new ads featuring a team of actors.
BT in the 1995/96 financial year spent about 60 million pounds on advertising.

The telecommunications company has said its increasing emphasis on advertising reflects the hotly competitive residential telephone market in Britain, where a host of other phone operators -- including cable television companies -- are marketing phone services.
